name: regkv
description: Read a Windows registry hive with regipy: a key's values (each with its registry type and length, read whole: regipy's default cut to 256 characters is not taken), its subkeys with their last-written times (raw FILETIME and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits), and a bounded recursive listing. A reader, not a decoder: a binary value comes back as hex and nothing more, so UserAssist, ShimCache, BAM, SAM and ShellBag values are not decoded here. Completeness is said: unreadable keys and values are under problems, branches the walk did not enter (depth or node limit, or an error) under stopped_branches, and the whole recursive listing is kept in a file the answer names past the inline page; status is complete or partial (partial when a problem was named, a branch was not entered, the inline listing was cut or the hive is dirty) and status_basis says which. Every key listed is also in a file the answer names (all_subkeys) when the inline list of 2,000 is not the whole of it. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. The tool stops at its own time limit (20 seconds, so that what it walked can be written and judged before the seal stop) with what it walked and names the first 1,000 branches it did not open (stopped_branches) and counts all of them (stopped_branch_count, stopped_branches_not_named); the clock is read for every subkey of the key being listed, and the subkeys of it that were not reached are counted (subkeys_not_listed_for_time), not listed or judged; tree_complete is true only when every key reached is in the inline listing (the first 2,000) and the walk was not stopped by its time limit, and is false otherwise (status says partial); SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. Problems are a page (the first 50 inline, all in the file all_problems names); A key that is not in a hive the tool read is an answer, not a failure: ok true, found false, exit 0, with deepest_found (how far the path matched; path_parts_matched of path_parts_asked), missing (the first part not found) and the names that are there (subkeys_there, at most 200; subkeys_there_count); its status is complete only when every subkey list on the way was read whole and the hive is not dirty, and partial with the reason otherwise. A key that was found says found true. A hive that is not there or cannot be read, and arguments that are wrong, stay failures (ok false, exit 1). A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. A value name that repeats is numbered once per name ('name (2)'). The library's own messages, which can hold bytes of a value or a name, are counted (library_messages_withheld) and never printed. depth is 0 to 128; a key whose subkey list was already reached (a cycle, or a list two keys share) is named and not entered again; a key that declares more values than were read is a problem; a hive that is not a regular file (a named pipe) is not opened. hive_dirty (the two sequence numbers differ), the log files looked for (transaction_logs_looked_for: the hive's name with .LOG1, .LOG2 and .LOG) and the ones beside the hive (transaction_logs_beside_hive) are reported; the logs are NOT replayed, so every answer from a dirty hive, a found key or a missing one, is partial and status_basis names the caveat (keys and values may differ from the live registry; registry_recover replays the logs on a copy). SENSITIVE: values whose name says password, secret, token or credential (a DWORD or QWORD excepted), every value under Policy\Secrets, PolEKList and PolSecretEncryptionKey of a SECURITY hive, the cached logons (NL$) and the V value of each SAM user are replaced by a marker holding only their length and listed under sensitive_values_withheld; the type of a value never lets one through, and the place is judged by the key names the hive holds, not by the spelling asked for. No flag brings one back. A secret inside a value that does not look like one (a command line with a password in it, an ImagePath) is NOT recognised and comes back whole. The key path is read from the hive's root, a leading backslash or not. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). ORDER: the subkeys of a key, the keys of a recursive listing, the values of a key and the names listed when a key is not found are in the order of the TEXT SHOWN for each name (a placeholder is its own text), and withheld names in an order of their own that is new for every run. The order the hive stores them in is not kept: a hive stores a key's subkeys alphabetically by their raw names, so a withheld name listed where the hive puts it would sit between its neighbours and give away its first letter. What a listing is ordered by is only what the answer shows. Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (key names, value names and value data): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (SEAL_BUDGET, 10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool, which is 3.5 seconds before its time limit because the string being judged at that point is finished first and one string of 256 KiB can take up to 2.3 seconds) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole by <withheld N bytes: backstop: the judging time ran out>, counted and listed, and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself (its keys, the names of its result files, the name of the hive, its status basis) and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token and, in a field of a typed kind (a SID, a GUID, a digest), fits the grammar of its type (so not a Slack-shaped token, not the value after a flag such as -pwd, not a prefix and 12 characters). The seal stop ends the judging only, not the tool's own work, which has its own, earlier clock. Putting a list in order and a contains filter judge under the same clock and cap of characters as an answer: past them, the names not yet judged come after the judged ones in an order of their own that is new for every run, a filter does not match in them, each is counted (boundary.strings_not_judged_for_order_or_filter) and the answer is partial. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: about 0.1% printed whole (0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 plants of the block's own harness; 1 of 105 canaries end to end, the same canary in four slots; an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940), so the rate is small and not zero. The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). The average hides channels: PowerShell/Operational has the XML of 25.0% of its 1,857 records replaced whole (script blocks carry base64 and long identifiers) and CodeIntegrity/Operational 33.3% of its 1,309 (event 3089, whose Hash is a padded base64 digest). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. INLINE VALUES: a value whose data is inside its record (four bytes at most) is read from the record for every registry type. regipy 6.3.0 reads up to 2 GiB of the hive file for such a value and returns that for a type it has no branch for (a device property under a Properties key, REG_LINK, REG_FILETIME, an unknown type), so one such value came back as megabytes of the hive; this tool replaces that read. BIG DATA AND REG_MULTI_SZ: the values of a key are read by this tool from regipy's copy of the hive, with regipy 6.3.0's records and names, and a value of more than 16,344 bytes that is kept in segments (a db record) is checked before its data is put together, whatever its type: one that declares more data than the hive file holds past its base block, whose list holds fewer segments than its size needs, runs past the end of the file or names one segment more than once, or one of whose segments lies past the end of the file or of its cell, is not read; it is named under problems by its place in the key's value list and its type, and the answer is partial (regipy put together whatever the list named: one 16 KB segment named 160 times was a 2.5 MiB value, and a 548 KB hive declared one of 2 GiB). Every value's data counts against the walk's data budget (four times the hive's size) before it is read. A value that declares more than 16 MiB of data is not read: it is named under problems with the length it declares. A value whose data runs past the end of the hive file or starts past it, or past the end of the cell that holds it (the bytes after it are the next cells', another value's among them), or that declares more than the four bytes its record holds, is not read: it is named under problems and the answer is partial (regipy gave the part inside the file, or nothing, or the next cells' bytes, as the whole value). VALUE TYPES: the bytes found are taken by one table, by type: REG_NONE, REG_BINARY, REG_RESOURCE_LIST, REG_FULL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR and REG_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_LIST are their bytes, whole; REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ and REG_LINK are UTF-16LE text without the NULs that end it, and data that is not valid UTF-16 is given as its bytes with a problem naming the first byte that does not decode; REG_DWORD (4 bytes), REG_DWORD_BIG_ENDIAN (4, read big-endian) and REG_QWORD (8) are numbers, and one of another size is not read; REG_FILETIME (8 bytes) is ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits, exact, and one past the year 9999 is given as its 8 bytes with a problem (regipy gave 1601-01-01); REG_MULTI_SZ is its strings, and strings after the empty one that ends the list are given and said; every other type (one Windows does not define, a device property 0xFFFF0000 + n, 0x00200000) is its bytes, whole, its type named by its number in decimal (regipy decoded such data as text, dropping trailing NULs, and named a device property by a registry type it is not). A value that is given as its bytes is printed as hex through the boundary. The values of a key are handed out one at a time and stop at 64 MiB of names and data for the key, said under problems. A subkey list keeps each key the first time it names it, and is read no further after 4,096 elements in a row that name keys it already named, or past 256 MiB of memory for its distinct keys (each counted with its record and its name, as stored and as decoded: a name can be 65,535 bytes), or once the names of the keys the walk kept add up to twice the hive's bytes (key cells that overlap, elements that point into other keys), each said under problems; a subkey list begun after the time limit is read to 16,384 elements and a value list to 4,096, and what is left is said. The hive is opened only when its base block and first bin are what regipy's open reads (the regf signature, a first bin of a positive multiple of 4096 bytes, the root cell the base block names inside the bins, allocated and a key, and the first allocated cell of the first bin that same cell): any other file is a failure that says what was found (regipy read a first bin of free space four bytes at a time, with no clock: a 40 MB hive took 58 s). A last-written FILETIME of more than 18 digits (past the year 5169) is withheld as a number and said under problems. A REG_MULTI_SZ is split by this tool in one pass and gives the strings regipy gives (empty ones left out); the bytes after its last NUL, and a string that is not valid UTF-16 with the rest of the data after it, are not in the answer, as with regipy, and are said under problems with their length (regipy dropped them without a word, and took 50 s on 2 MiB with no NUL). The tool's deadline is read before every value and every 256 subkey elements of a list begun before it: the values or subkeys of a key that were not read in time are said under problems. A key that declares more values than were read says so, and says how many of them this tool did not read.

hive.description: Path to the registry hive file on disk (a copy; transaction logs beside it are named, not applied)

key.description: Registry key path, backslash form e.g. \Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion

depth.description: Levels below the key to open when recurse=true (default 2); a branch left closed is listed under stopped_branches

limit.description: Recursive nodes shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole listing is in the file named by all_nodes

max_nodes.description: Upper bound on the nodes a recursive walk visits (default 1000000); branches left past it are listed under stopped_branches

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
